name: What is the difference between a gazebo and a pergola?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a gazebo and a pergola?

acceptedAnswer.text: While both gazebos and pergolas provide outdoor shade, they differ in structure and function. A gazebo is typically a freestanding, octagonal or circular structure with a solid, often pitched, roof providing full protection from sun and rain. A pergola, on the other hand, usually features a flat, open slat roof supported by columns, offering partial shade and often used to define pathways or frame outdoor seating areas. Gazebos are more enclosed, offering a room-like feel.
acceptedAnswer.description: Gazebos have solid roofs for full protection and an enclosed feel, while pergolas have open slat roofs providing partial shade.
